protections: Out-direction mapping (Camel message to HTTP): protocol/common header names and Camel-prefixed names must be dropped before they reach an Undertow request or response, via HttpUtil.addCommonFilters plus UndertowHeaderFilterStrategy.setOutFilterStartsWith (components/camel-undertow/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/component/undertow/UndertowHeaderFilterStrategy.java:29-35; core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/http/HttpUtil.java:126-141).

In-direction mapping (HTTP to Camel message): the same strategy must decide for request headers, response headers, query parameters and form fields before they become Camel message headers (components/camel-undertow/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/component/undertow/DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:143-147, 232-235, 251-254, 323-329).

The strategy actually consulted must be the one configured on the endpoint doing the exchange (the undertow default, a user strategy, or the REST-specific one), not a stale or neighbouring UndertowHttpBinding instance's copy (components/camel-undertow/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/component/undertow/UndertowEndpoint.java:316-325).

traps.note: The filter decision is taken by the UndertowHttpBinding object (DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:425-429 and 352-355 read its own field), but the endpoint copies its strategy into a binding only at lazy creation (UndertowEndpoint.java:316-325): a binding supplied through the component (UndertowComponent.java:127-129) or created before the strategy is later set (UndertowComponent.java:331-333) keeps its own strategy and the endpoint's is never consulted.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Every DefaultUndertowHttpBinding already installs an UndertowHeaderFilterStrategy (DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:86), so filtering still happens, and a custom binding can be argued to own its own filtering.

traps.note: The REST consumer route installs a fresh RestUndertowHttpBinding and never hands the endpoint's configured strategy to it, so the binding's own default is the only strategy in play (RestUndertowHttpBinding.java:31-33 into DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:85-90).
traps.reason_to_dismiss: RestUndertowHttpBinding extends DefaultUndertowHttpBinding, so it already carries the same undertow-specific default strategy; only a differently configured strategy is lost.

traps.note: The REST producer overwrites whatever strategy the endpoint already had with a newly constructed UndertowRestHeaderFilterStrategy, with no resolution of a configured strategy first, whereas the netty-http twin resolves one and only then falls back (components/camel-netty-http/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/component/netty/http/NettyHttpComponent.java:508-514).
traps.reason_to_dismiss: UndertowRestHeaderFilterStrategy is what keeps URI-template and query-parameter names from being filtered out of the request (UndertowRestHeaderFilterStrategy.java:34-37 and HttpUtil.java:239-255), so substituting a user strategy would break REST parameter mapping.

traps.note: Only the out-direction prefix filter is configured (UndertowHeaderFilterStrategy.java:35), so the in-direction mapping accepts request header names that begin with Camel or org.apache.camel. and they land in the Camel message (DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:232-235), where internal headers such as the response-code header are read (HttpUtil.java:55) and the path header steers the outbound URI (UndertowHelper.java:62-76); the netty-http and vertx-http strategies configure both directions.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Adding the in filter as written would also filter the CamelAuthentication marker that DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:220-223 sets for Basic auth, and the deprecated PlatformHttpHeaderFilterStrategy.java:43 also sets only the out filter.

traps.note: The producer writes the request Host header straight from the Camel message header (UndertowProducer.java:135-140, value keyed by UndertowConstants.HOST_STRING at UndertowConstants.java:67-68) instead of consulting the strategy, so the host entry that the HTTP common deny-list puts in the out filter (HttpUtil.java:129) is never used for the header it names.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: preserveHostHeader defaults to true and is documented as the reverse-proxy behaviour that forwards the incoming Host header (UndertowEndpoint.java:126-131), so removing the message-driven Host breaks a supported feature.

traps.note: Content-Type is written to the request and the response outside the strategy at three sites even though content-type is in the out deny-list (HttpUtil.java:128), and the in-direction mapping also copies the request Content-Type into the Camel message (DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:212-214), so the value can round-trip from request to response.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Content-Type must stay settable for the component to work at all, and whether a value can carry a header break depends on Undertow's own encoder checks, which are outside this repository.

traps.note: Path-template values are written into the Camel message headers without consulting the strategy, both from the Undertow predicate context (DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:259-271) and from the REST placeholder evaluation (RestUndertowHttpBinding.java:48-53 into HttpHelper.java:146-176).
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The header names come from the application's own URI template rather than from the request, so only the values are caller-controlled.

masking: Fixing T1 makes T3 decisive: while the binding never takes the endpoint's strategy, the REST producer's overwrite at UndertowComponent.java:333 cannot change the filter in use; once T1 is fixed, that overwrite is what decides.

A broad in-direction filter for T4 also removes the inbound Host and Content-Type round-trip that T5 and T6 consume, so a T4-only fix hides those two paths for proxied messages while leaving the route-set variants reachable.

conflicts.what: The natural T3 fix (honour the endpoint's configured strategy in the REST producer) drops the template and query parameter headers unless the REST filterCheck exemption is preserved (UndertowRestHeaderFilterStrategy.java:34-37, HttpUtil.java:239-255), which is exactly the unfiltered path T7 records.

The natural T1 fix (push the endpoint's strategy into every binding) overrides the strategy a custom or REST binding was constructed with (DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:103-106), so a fix has to choose which object wins; the binding's own strategy may be deliberate.

fairness_risks: preserveHostHeader=true is a documented reverse-proxy behaviour that forwards the incoming Host header (UndertowEndpoint.java:126-131); a rule that forbids a message-driven Host breaks it.

Basic-auth detection depends on the CamelAuthentication key passing the in-direction filter (DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:220-223); a blanket Camel-prefix in filter blocks that marker unless the block is reordered as the netty binding does (DefaultNettyHttpBinding.java:197-203).

REST producers need URI-template and query-parameter names to stay unfiltered (UndertowRestHeaderFilterStrategy.java:34-37, HttpUtil.java:239-255); a strict user filter without that exemption breaks REST parameter mapping.
Content-Type, Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding must remain settable although they are in the deny-list (HttpUtil.java:126-141).
A user-supplied UndertowHttpBinding may deliberately configure its own strategy (DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:103-106); forcing the endpoint's overrides it.

A request-shape a legitimate proxy use relies on: a message-level CamelHttpPath or CamelHttpQuery header is how UndertowHelper.java:62-76 and 92-111 let a message steer the outbound URI, so refusing every inbound Camel-prefixed name also refuses that shape.

design.why: Four independent groups, four different reasons to dismiss, all reachable from the header-filter strategy the advisories name. T1 is the report's own route (the endpoint's strategy never reaches the binding that filters), T3 is the REST producer's coupled-value case MiMo over-hardens, T4 is an absent-direction protection with a strong dismissal (it would break Basic auth) that DeepSeek tends to skip, and T5 is a bypassed path protected by a documented feature. Each can be verified by a separate behavioural test, they do not share a fix site, and they avoid T6/T7 where the observable impact depends on Undertow's own value encoding or on application-chosen template names. Candidate sub-status was H3b2 (incomplete earlier fix rather than a regression): the pinned state already carries the undertow-specific default at UndertowEndpoint.java:87 and DefaultUndertowHttpBinding.java:86, while the discard logic at UndertowEndpoint.java:262-264 and 316-325 was left outside the earlier fix.
